blockers.quote: The fact lands on you: the Tail End arithmetic on in-person time left with parents
blockers.why: story #7: The fact arrives before you act on the wrong belief. Skipping the festival must happen first so the arithmetic breaks your belief in “later.”
blockers.fix: Reorder the beat: you skip the festival because there will always be another visit; Mom’s counter falls while you are absent; then one sourced Tail End fact explains why “later” contains fewer in-person days than you assumed.

blockers.quote: mom named at 0:00, warm beats before
blockers.why: story #9: The outline asserts warm beats but names none. A weekend home is not enough to earn Mom as the person at stake.
blockers.fix: Add two concrete warm moments before the loss: Mom keeps chai waiting on your first weekend home, then quietly packs food for the return train. Echo one of them immediately before the missed festival.

blockers.quote: You call more, visit more, and the counter climbs: it was never her clock, only yours.
blockers.why: No new power rule after the halfway point: this first reveals after 65% that choices can raise the forecast. Calls also conflict with the stated in-person rule.
blockers.fix: Before midpoint, state: “It is a forecast of in-person meetings, recalculated whenever your plans change.” At the late payoff, replace calling more with taking more trains home and choosing the nearer transfer.

suggestions.quote: The metro stranger: four hundred (your commute). The annoying colleague: three thousand. Your crush: two.
suggestions.fix: Turn the three-number list into escalating actions with surprises: hide from the colleague and end up seated beside them; message the crush and get the bubble “Who is this?”

suggestions.quote: Does a video call count? Does she have a counter for me? Why only forty-two?
suggestions.fix: Answer these where introduced: say calls do not count because the rule is in-person, briefly show Mom’s reciprocal counter, and tie forty-two to the single sourced arithmetic line.

suggestions.quote: the next time you leave home, turn round at the corner
suggestions.fix: Avoid the teacher-like instruction and end with the question: “Next time you leave, who will you turn back for?”

keep.quote: counter hangs over her head: forty-two, the times you will see her again.
A whole metro carriage of counters, every one falling a little as the doors close
you cannot make it endless, you can only make it larger
